outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Large Context Windows and Their Challenges
outline.description: An introductory overview establishing why expanding the context window of Large Language Models (LLMs) is critical for advanced AI applications, followed by a discussion of the historical limitations (approx. 128k tokens) and the specific technical barriers preventing further expansion.
subtopics: The importance of long context windows for in-context learning and agent workflows
Current limits of pre-trained LLMs (e.g., LLaMA2's 4k limit)
Three primary obstacles to extreme extension:
- Catastrophic values in untrained new positions causing OOD issues
- Scarcity of ultra-long text data (>1000k tokens)

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Foundations of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)
outline.description: A deep dive into the mathematical mechanics of RoPE, the dominant positional embedding scheme in modern LLMs, explaining how it encodes relative distances and defining the core parameters involved in context extension strategies.
subtopics: Mathematical formulation of RoPE: Rotation matrices and frequencies ($\theta_i$)
Defining the Extension Ratio ($s$): Target length vs. Original length
Mechanics of Linear Position Interpolation (PI): How it downscales angles and causes 'crowding'
Limitations of uniform interpolation at high extension ratios

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Evolutionary Approaches to Position Interpolation
outline.description: An examination of prior art attempting to fix Pi's failures, including NTK-aware methods and YaRN, analyzing their reliance on heuristic rules versus adaptive search methods.
subtopics: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) Theory application to RoPE dimensions
- Differentiating between high-frequency (lower dims) and low-frequency (higher dims) treatment
- Limitations of hand-crafted heuristics and rule-based grouping
- Why existing non-linear methods still fail at >10x extension ratios
